original_question: We say that a group is a Tarski monster if it is finitely generated, not cyclic, and all of its proper non-trivial subgroups are isomorphic to each other. a) Do there exist amenable torsion-free Tarski monsters? b) Do there exist amenable Tarski monsters of prime exponent?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.72 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of The Kourovka Notebook: the two existence questions about amenable Tarski monsters, one torsion-free and one of prime exponent.
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely faithful to the paper. It reproduces the paper's definition of a Tarski monster—finitely generated, non-cyclic, with all proper non-trivial subgroups isomorphic to each other—and it preserves the exact two-part existence problem asked in the paper: amenable torsion-free Tarski monsters, and amenable Tarski monsters of prime exponent.
missing_details: Make explicit in part (b) that "of prime exponent" means "of exponent p for some prime p"; the paper does not fix the prime in advance.
Make explicit that parts (a) and (b) are two separate existence questions, not one request for a single example satisfying both conditions simultaneously.
refined_question: Let G be a group. Call G a Tarski monster if G is finitely generated, non-cyclic, and every proper non-trivial subgroup of G is isomorphic to every other proper non-trivial subgroup of G. Do there exist amenable Tarski monsters in either of the following two cases: (a) G is torsion-free; (b) G has exponent p for some prime p?
justification: The draft is targeting exactly Problem 21.72. The paper introduces the term "Tarski monster" with precisely this definition and then asks, as parts (a) and (b), whether there exist amenable torsion-free Tarski monsters and amenable Tarski monsters of prime exponent. There is no theorem/proposition nearby giving a sharper equivalent reformulation, so the best paper-faithful refinement is essentially the official wording, with only the implicit quantifier in "prime exponent" made explicit.
